variables.name: Air temperature
variables.definition: How warm the air is about two metres above the ground, averaged over a month.

possible_causes.text: More greenhouse gases in the atmosphere hold in heat.
Less vegetation means less cooling from evaporation.
Changes in cloud cover alter how much sunlight reaches the ground.
Cities and farmland absorb and release heat differently from forests.

variables.name: Precipitation
variables.definition: How much rain and snow falls, added up over a month.

possible_causes.text: Shifting wind belts move storm tracks away from a region.
A warmer atmosphere can carry more water vapour.
Changes in ocean temperature alter where rain forms.
Rain shadows and mountains change where clouds drop their water.

variables.name: Soil moisture
variables.definition: How much water is held in the top 10 centimetres of soil, where plant roots start, measured as millimetres of water.

possible_causes.text: Less rain means less water soaks into the soil.
Hotter air pulls more water out of the soil through evaporation.
Farming and irrigation change how much water the soil holds.
Melting snow and ice add water to the soil in spring.

variables.name: Vegetation index (NDVI)
variables.definition: A satellite measure of how green and leafy the land is. It has no units: about 0 for bare rock, sand or snow, and close to 1 for dense, healthy plants.

possible_causes.text: Plants grow more when there is more rain and soil water.
A longer warm season gives plants more time to grow.
Clearing forests for farms or towns removes plant cover.
Droughts and fires cut back plant growth.

method_citation: Acker, J. G., McMahon, E., Shen, S., Hearty, T. and Casey, N. (2009). Time-series analysis of remotely-sensed SeaWiFS chlorophyll in river-influenced coastal regions. EARSeL eProceedings 8(2), 114-139.
